findings.message: Composite action interpolates input(s) who directly into a shell command (step: 'unnamed'). Any caller passing untrusted text (a PR title, branch name, comment) gets command injection. Map inputs to env: and quote the variables.
Composite action uses sub-action 'actions/setup-node@main' without full commit SHA pinning. Tags and branches are mutable and pose security risks.
Job 'scan' appears to be read-only but its GITHUB_TOKEN has write permissions (set at the job level). Grant write only to jobs that need it.
Job 'options' GITHUB_TOKEN has write permissions: security-events
Job 'scan' GITHUB_TOKEN has write permissions: security-events

Action 'actions/checkout' is used with different versions (3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1, v3) across 2 workflow file(s). This can lead to inconsistent behavior and security vulnerabilities.
Workflow uses write-all permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN. This grants excessive access and significantly increases the attack surface.
Job 'deploy' performs sensitive operations that should have detailed audit logging. Insufficient logging makes forensic analysis difficult.
Job 'deploy' uses long-term AWS credentials (input 'aws-access-key-id') instead of OIDC. Long-term credentials are less secure and harder to rotate.
Job 'deploy' contains curl piped to shell. This pattern can execute malicious code downloaded from the internet.
Action 'aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4' uses version tag 'v4' instead of an immutable commit SHA hash. Tags can be moved or overwritten, creating a security risk.
Action 'actions/checkout@v3' uses version tag 'v3' instead of an immutable commit SHA hash. Tags can be moved or overwritten, creating a security risk.
Workflow has write permissions to repository contents. This increases the attack surface if the workflow is compromised.
Job 'deploy' passes user-controllable context to an action input (step: 'unnamed'): github.event.head_commit.message. Confirm the action treats this input as data and does not execute it.
Job 'deploy' gates behaviour on github.actor/github.triggering_actor. The actor context is spoofable in several trigger contexts and is not a reliable trust boundary.
Job 'deploy' makes outbound network connections with no egress filtering configured. If a step or dependency is compromised, nothing restricts where it can send credentials or data.
